## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Ussayavādikā* ("The training rule on taking legal action") is the first rule in the *saṅghādisesa* category of the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* in the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule stipulates that a nun who engages in inappropriate or contentious legal action against another party is subject to suspension, requiring formal meetings of the Community (*saṅghādisesa*) for rehabilitation [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the rule and its associated analysis is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this training rule is shared widely across early Buddhist monastic traditions. Within the Pali canon, it corresponds to the first *saṅghādisesa* in the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (*pli-tv-bi-pm-ss1*) and the *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* (*Saṅghādisesa 1*) [SuttaCentral]. Across other Vinaya lineages, parallel rules are preserved in Chinese translations of the Dharmaguptaka (*Lzh Dg Bi Vb Ss 4* and its *pātimokkha*), Mahīśāsaka (*Lzh Mi Bi Vb Ss 7*), Sarvāstivāda (*Lzh Sarv Bi Vb Ss 7*), and Mahāsaṅghika (*Lzh Mg Bi Vb Ss 4*), as well as in Sanskrit versions of the Lokottaravāda (*san-lo-bi-vb-ss4*) and Sarvāstivāda (*san-sarv-bi-vb-ss7*) traditions [SuttaCentral].

Text-reuse computations from DharmaNexus record 544 matching passages between this text and 93 other Pali canonical and paracanonical works [DharmaNexus]. Its highest levels of formulaic overlap occur with *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pārājika 2*, *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 3* and *2*, the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha*, and various *Nissaggiya Pācittiya* rules, representing recurring legal and expository Vinaya vocabulary [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language machine alignments by DharmaNexus also detect text reuse in the Sanskrit *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* and Tibetan Vinaya collections, corroborating the cross-tradition parallels cataloged on SuttaCentral [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral].
